content:
I've been cooking a new platform for native macOS apps and would love any help from people testing it. Packaging everything up for a platform release and getting that working reliably across every machine can be finicky but I think I've got something working nicely now.

If you have a mac (Intel or Apple silicon) could you please try and report if it works for you (and what your system is)

curl -LO https://github.com/lukewilliamboswell/roc-native-macos/releases/download/0.0.2/macos.roc
roc macos.roc init my-app
cd my-app
roc macos.roc run

That should start up the starter template app.

Here's the GH link -- it's definitely an early or WIP as there are many missing features and I need to spend a lot more time polishing the Swift and examples/docs.

https://github.com/lukewilliamboswell/roc-native-macos

I dont have an intel mac available... so I'm thinking there might be an issue somewhere there.

If you could test the packaging a release build (I dont expect you to add Apple Developer for code signing, but if you do that would be eipc to know) -- you should get a proper universal app package.

I'm also only 99% confident in the linker inputs and symbols or configuration will just work* for every machine. I think most modern mac's should work but I haven't spent enough time mapping that out to say which versions should work or not
Works beautifully on my MacBook (Apple Silicon)
Same here! Can't wait to start building on this platform. Nice work Luke!
Awesome, I might polish it a little more and try and put a video introduction or something together for a blog post.

I ran roc macos.roc package which created ./dist/my-app-0.1.0.zip. I unzipped it and drag & dropped the app into my /Applications folder, and surprisingly I got no warning at all when I started the app. I don't know how MacOS security works, but I guess it figured out that I built it so I must trust it?
Yes I think thats right. I don't understand it enough either
I also have no idea how I'm going to test the x64 v1 cpu variant... but hopefully someone has an old intel mac
